However, phd-engineering-computational-math has career_goal_tags=null in the taxonomy, so it structurally cannot match a 'professor' career query at all, even though pursuing a professorship via an engineering PhD is a realistic path. This is the documented null-career-tags limitation, not a new finding (see DISC-014/015's data_status='manual_required' provenance — fabricating a career tag here would violate the no-speculative-information principle).

Phase 3A.5 observation (not acted on): select_recommendation()'s general-fallback multi_recommend path also hardcodes a top-2 cap (medium_programs[:2]), so even if Engineering PhD someday gained a real career_goal_tags entry, a 3-candidate tie could still only ever surface 2 programs. Not changed — no current eval case exercises a genuine 3-way tie, and generalizing the cap now would be speculative engineering against a hypothetical taxonomy change, not a fix for this case.

This eliminates the prior scoring artifact (an unrelated engineering program no longer surfaces for a healthcare query), but does not reach the ideal outcome of a confident drph-public-health match, since distinguishing 'research orientation is closer to applied than to clinical' would require a scoring-model change (degree-of-mismatch, not just match/mismatch), which is out of scope for override-architecture work.
cases.rationale: Traced exactly: with the override now scoped to taxonomy-matched candidates, phd-engineering-computational-math is never considered at all for this background-driven gap, removing the off-domain artifact; the remaining gap is a scoring-model limitation, not an override-architecture one.
cases.notes: Phase 3A.5 review reconfirms this classification: this is a true (if narrow) architectural limitation — the scoring model treats orientation mismatch as flat/binary rather than a question of relative distance — not an intentional design choice or a taxonomy limitation. Still the most significant scoring-related finding from this audit, and still explicitly out of scope: this phase's non-goals forbid heuristic-weight/scoring-model changes, and 'research is closer to applied than to clinical' would require exactly that. A strong candidate for a dedicated future scoring-model phase.
